parameters.label: General Settings
parameters.description: General settings involving the message system.

fields.label: Default Rows
fields.description: Default number of rows to display for the Message Window.

fields.label: Default Width
fields.description: Default Message Window width in pixels.

fields.label: Fast Forward Key
fields.description: This is the key used for fast forwarding messages.

fields.label: Text Delay
fields.description: How many frames to wait between characters drawn?

fields.label: Offset X
fields.description: Message window horizontal offset in pixels; positive right and negative left.
fields.context: Enable Coreto_0_CoreEngine then Coreto_1_MessageCore. Configure /General/MsgWindowOffsetX as a JSON number through message parameters set, selecting the intended MZ game with --project. Reload the editor/restart after parameter edits. Initializes the saved game-system x offset. Normal placement starts from horizontal centering in the game box and adds it, then clamps to the full game screen/box margins. Auto-target placement also adds it; an explicit forced x overrides ordinary placement. Existing saves retain their stored offset; use MessageWindowXyOffsets to change current game state.

examples.expected: Previews the illustrative value 12; remove --dry-run to apply the validated configuration.

fields.label: Offset Y
fields.description: Message window vertical offset in pixels; positive down and negative up.
fields.context: Enable Coreto_0_CoreEngine then Coreto_1_MessageCore. Configure /General/MsgWindowOffsetY as a JSON number through message parameters set, selecting the intended MZ game with --project. Reload the editor/restart after parameter edits. Initializes the saved game-system y offset. Normal placement starts from the Show Text top/middle/bottom position and adds it, then clamps to the full game screen/box margins. Auto-target placement also adds it; an explicit forced y overrides ordinary placement. Existing saves retain their stored offset; use MessageWindowXyOffsets to change current game state.

examples.expected: Previews the illustrative value -8; remove --dry-run to apply the validated configuration.

fields.label: Stretch Dimmed BG
fields.description: Stretch dimmed window background to fit the whole screen.

fields.label: Default Outline Width
fields.description: Changes the default outline width to this many pixels thick.

fields.label: Each Message Start
fields.description: This is text that is added at the start of each message.

fields.label: Each Message End
fields.description: This is text that is added at the end of each message.

fields.label: Default Color
fields.description: Default color for the Name Box Window's text.
fields.context: Color numbers refer to the current img/system/Window.png windowskin palette, not a universal named-color table. It has 32 cells in four rows of eight, starting at palette coordinate (96,144); index n samples pixel (96+(n%8)*12+6,144+floor(n/8)*12+6). Thus 0 is the first cell and 8 the first cell of the second row. A custom windowskin changes the actual colors. Configure the relevant numeric index; no new color asset is created. Default text color in the Name Box Window; a text color escape in the speaker text takes precedence.

fields.label: Offset X
fields.description: Name-box horizontal offset setting in pixels, adjusted by speaker alignment.
fields.context: Enable Coreto_0_CoreEngine then Coreto_1_MessageCore. Configure /General/NameBoxWindowOffsetX as a JSON number through message parameters set, selecting the intended MZ game with --project. Reload the editor/restart after parameter edits. For non-RTL text, alignment position n uses floor(offset*(5-n)/5) after relative placement: n=0 left gives +offset, n=5 center gives 0, n=10 right gives -offset. Position n comes from speaker LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT or POSITION tag. Positive offset therefore moves a left-aligned box right but a right-aligned box left. Screen clamps apply. RTL keeps its native placement path plus the base offset rather than this relative-alignment calculation.

examples.expected: Previews the illustrative value 12; remove --dry-run to apply the validated configuration.

fields.label: Offset Y
fields.description: Name-box vertical offset in pixels; positive down and negative up from native placement.
fields.context: Enable Coreto_0_CoreEngine then Coreto_1_MessageCore. Configure /General/NameBoxWindowOffsetY as a JSON number through message parameters set, selecting the intended MZ game with --project. Reload the editor/restart after parameter edits. Added after the native name-box updatePlacement chooses above/below the message. Screen clamp then applies. If the name box overlaps the top of the message under the provider overlap test, it is moved below the message. The field changes name-box placement, not message height or text cursor y.

examples.expected: Previews the illustrative value 4; remove --dry-run to apply the validated configuration.

fields.label: Line Height
fields.description: Choice row line-height setting in pixels; actual item height adds 8 pixels.
fields.context: Enable Coreto_0_CoreEngine then Coreto_1_MessageCore. Configure /General/ChoiceWindowLineHeight as a JSON number through message parameters set, selecting the intended MZ game with --project. Reload the editor/restart after parameter edits. Initializes the saved choice line-height setting. A value of 36 yields itemHeight=44. Use a finite positive value large enough for the text/icons; no extra clamp is added by the getter. Multiple lines and font sizes still determine drawn text height. Change current-game setting with ChoiceWindowProperties LineHeight; existing saves retain their value.

examples.expected: Previews the illustrative value 36; remove --dry-run to apply the validated configuration.

fields.label: Minimum Choice Width
fields.description: Minimum per-choice content width in pixels before window padding and columns.
fields.context: Enable Coreto_0_CoreEngine then Coreto_1_MessageCore. Configure /General/ChoiceWindowMinWidth as a JSON number through message parameters set, selecting the intended MZ game with --project. Reload the editor/restart after parameter edits. Initializes a saved width floor. The renderer uses at least 1 pixel, any larger CHOICE WIDTH tag, and measured text plus item padding. Column count/spacing/window padding then contribute to window width, capped to Graphics.width. Use a finite nonnegative value; this is not a fixed overall window width. ChoiceWindowProperties MinWidth changes current game state.

examples.expected: Previews the illustrative value 160; remove --dry-run to apply the validated configuration.

parameters.context: Configure startup message and window settings. CLI parameters get returns decoded JSON. Setting /General requires the complete object, including all defined fields; it does not merge a partial object. To preserve sibling values, set one child path such as /General/MessageRows instead. Reload the editor after a CLI write and restart the game to reload plugin settings.

fields.label: \C[1]: Blue
fields.description: Words automatically wrapped in windowskin palette color 1 in supported formatted-text windows.
fields.context: Enable Coreto_0_CoreEngine then Coreto_1_MessageCore. Configure /AutoColor/TextColor1 as a JSON array of strings, for example ["Potion"], using message parameters set with --project selecting the MZ game. Reload the editor/restart after editing. Message, Help, ChoiceList and an available TextPopup use automatic coloring. Latin entries match case-sensitively at word boundaries, globally; entries containing recognized CJK/symbol characters match a case-insensitive literal occurrence without word boundaries and without the global flag. Empty/numeric-only entries are ignored. Rules compile by ascending palette index and descending word length inside each color, and run sequentially; overlapping entries can therefore wrap earlier replacements, so keep a word in one color list for predictable output. Database-name rules join these lists; live actor-name coloring runs afterwards. COLORLOCK blocks drawing-time color changes. Existing palette cells come from img/system/Window.png; this field does not change the RGB colors. See message api describe MSG-BEH-autocolor --json for the full pipeline.

examples.input: message parameters set --path /AutoColor/TextColor1 --value '["Potion"]' --dry-run --json; after applying/restarting, MZ Show Text: Potion.
examples.expected: The preview validates the illustrative word list. Applied configuration colors Potion with palette index 1 in an eligible unlocked text window.

parameters.context: Applies to message, help and choice windows (and an available text-popup window). TextColor1 through TextColor31 are literal keyword lists; color 0 disables database highlighting. Latin keywords use case-sensitive whole-word matching and replace every match. Keywords containing CJK or the supported symbol ranges use case-insensitive substring matching of the first occurrence. Lists run in ascending color order, with longer names first within a list; later rules can match text already colored. Avoid duplicate or overlapping keywords when choosing a single color. Actor names are processed afterwards. Set a child path to preserve other lists; replacing /AutoColor requires the complete object.

parameters.label: Custom Font Manager
parameters.description: Register font families and files loaded from the game's fonts/ directory during boot.

fields.label: Font Family
fields.description: Family name registered for the file, then used by text rendering.
fields.context: Configure one /CustomFonts row with FontFamily="StoryFont" and Filename="StoryFont.ttf", then provide fonts/StoryFont.ttf. Both names are illustrative; use the actual family/file you supply. Empty or Unnamed families and the filename Unnamed.ttf are ignored at boot. This loads/registers the family but does not select it for drawing; use the same family in the desired font setting and restart the game.

fields.label: Filename
fields.description: Font filename including extension, relative to the game's fonts/ directory.
fields.context: Configure one /CustomFonts row with FontFamily="StoryFont" and Filename="StoryFont.ttf", then provide fonts/StoryFont.ttf. Both names are illustrative; use the actual family/file you supply. Empty or Unnamed families and the filename Unnamed.ttf are ignored at boot. This loads/registers the family but does not select it for drawing; use the same family in the desired font setting and restart the game.

parameters.context: Add a complete {"FontFamily":"StoryFont","Filename":"StoryFont.ttf"} item to CustomFonts and place that actual font file in fonts/. The filename includes its extension. Loading uses the runtime FontFace implementation, so use a font format it can decode (for example a valid .ttf); the plugin does not convert fonts. Blank or Unnamed families and the placeholder Unnamed.ttf are skipped. Registration alone does not change the text font. With the default FontChange action retained, Show Text: \FontChange<StoryFont>Hello\ResetFont. Restart the game after editing the list.

fields.context: Configure one /TextCodeActions row with Match="MARK", Type="", CommonEvent=0 and ActionJS="const state=arguments[0]; this.contents.fontBold=true;". In Show Text use \MARKBold text. Match is regex source after the escape marker, case-insensitive; prefer an alphabetic name without regex metacharacters or a built-in escape name. Rules normalize longest Match first, while dispatch compares the uppercased Match to the parsed code. Type empty adds a synthetic [0] that the dispatcher consumes. For a numeric argument use nonempty Type and text \MARK[3]; ActionJS can call this.obtainEscapeParam(state), which consumes the bracketed integer and returns an empty string if absent. For a string use \MARK<hello> and this.obtainEscapeString(state), which consumes the angle-bracket string and returns empty if absent. Action Type does not append its regex to the conversion matcher. ActionJS is a function body with this=the text window and arguments[0]=textState (text,index,x,y,startX,startY,drawing,buffer among its fields). It runs during drawing and measurement; guard side effects with state.drawing. CommonEvent runs only during real Window_Message drawing on a map, not measurement or battle, requires an existing event ID, and starts a separate map-updated interpreter without blocking the message. Multiple triggers can overlap; map initialization/setupEvents clears them and completion removes finished interpreters; loading preserves a serialized array and initializes it only if absent. Zero disables the event.

parameters.context: Register complete action records, then invoke their Match as an escape code in Show Text. Example item: {"Match":"Signal","Type":"","CommonEvent":1,"ActionJS":"const state = arguments[0];"}; use \Signal to run existing Common Event 1. CommonEvent 0 disables launch. ActionJS runs first with this bound to the text window and arguments[0] equal to its text state; it can run during measurement, so guard game side effects with state.drawing. After ActionJS, CommonEvent launches only while drawing in an exact Window_Message, outside battle using a parallel map interpreter; a missing common event is ignored. Type empty needs no authored argument; for parameterized actions consume the argument from the text state yourself. Match is case-insensitive; actions sharing a Match all run in array order and may consume the same state sequentially. Built-in handled codes take precedence; use a distinct alphabetic Match. Setting the whole array replaces it: read, append complete records, then set to preserve the existing actions.

fields.label: Enable Switching?
fields.description: Enable language switching settings for this plugin?
fields.context:
Requires /Localization/Enable=true and a nonempty Languages array. Place the configured basename Languages.csv or Languages.tsv in the game root, beside index.html, not data/. CSV uses semicolons; TSV uses tabs. UTF-8 header starts Key followed by language column names such as English and Portuguese. Each row must have the same number of cells; keys and column names must be nonempty and unique after case/whitespace normalization. Use
inside cells instead of physical newlines. Example CSV: Key;English;Portuguese followed by a new row Greeting;Hello;Ola. Author Show Text as $[Greeting] or \KEY[Greeting]. Key lookup ignores case/outer whitespace, but language-column lookup uses the exact configured locale spelling after trimming the header. A missing key returns undefined (explicit replacement can render "undefined"); a missing/empty language cell renders UNDEFINED!, not an English fallback. HTTP/parse failure stops database readiness with a load error; no file is created by the runtime. See MSG-BEH-language-write-boundary for CLI create/convert/validate commands.

parameters.label: Language Images
parameters.description: Choose image filename markers for each active language.

fields.label: Convert Default?
fields.description: ON: Default language uses converted marker.
fields.context: Requires localization enabled. ImageManager.loadBitmap replaces the exact uppercase marker [XX] in its filename argument (which may include subfolders), not in its separate folder argument. It substitutes the selected language string when ConvertDefault=true or the current locale differs from DefaultLocale. Example: show picture "Title_[XX]", set /LanguageImages/Portuguese="pt", and select Portuguese; img/pictures/Title_pt.png must exist. A marker in a filename subpath such as "[XX]/Title" resolves img/pictures/pt/Title.png. Empty/missing mapping leaves [XX] unchanged. There is no automatic fallback to the default-language asset if a resolved file is missing; normal image-load failure applies. Install all required assets. This does not translate image pixels or generate files.

A marker in a filename subpath such as "[XX]/Title" resolves img/pictures/pt/Title.png. Empty/missing mapping leaves [XX] unchanged. There is no automatic fallback to the default-language asset if a resolved file is missing; normal image-load failure applies. Install all required assets. This does not translate image pixels or generate files.

Reload the editor/restart after parameter edits. The wrapping boundary subtracts this value from available text width before face adjustments. Use a finite nonnegative value smaller than the usable width; runtime adds no clamp, so a negative value expands allowance and an oversized value forces early breaks/overflow rather than resizing the window. entries.context: Register replacement records and invoke them with a backslash in text. Example item: {"Match":"Greeting","Type":"","TextStr":"Hello!","TextJS":"return 'Fallback';"}; Show Text \Greeting yields Hello!. A nonempty TextStr other than the exact sentinel Undefined wins; only otherwise is TextJS called. In TextJS, this is the converting window; arguments are the String.replace callback arguments (full match, captures, offset, input, plus named groups if present). Match and Type form a case-insensitive global regular expression; escape regex metacharacters when a literal is intended. Rules run by descending Match-string length, preserving input order for equal lengths; later rules can process earlier output. JavaScript can be called during measurement too, so use it to return text without game side effects. Setting the whole array replaces it: read, append complete records, then set to preserve prior rules.

entries.description: Text codes that replace themselves with text.

entries.title: plugin/TextMacros:arraystruct
entries.context: Register macro records, then use [Match] without a backslash. Example item: {"Match":"Greeting","TextStr":"Hello!","TextJS":"return 'Fallback';"}; Show Text [Greeting] yields Hello!. A nonempty TextStr other than the exact sentinel Undefined wins; otherwise TextJS supplies the text. In TextJS, this is the converting window; arguments are the String.replace callback arguments (full match, captures, offset, input, plus named groups if present). Match is embedded in a case-insensitive global regular expression within literal brackets, so avoid regex metacharacters for simple names. Macros run in array order; later macros can process earlier output and duplicate matches may already have been replaced. JavaScript can run during measurement, so keep it free of game side effects. Setting the whole array replaces it: read, append complete records, then set to preserve existing macros.
entries.expected: Estrutura TextMacros aplica os campos filhos mapeados individualmente; array conserva ordem, nomes e defaults de cada entrada.

entries.title: plugin/Localization:struct
entries.context:
Requires /Localization/Enable=true and a nonempty Languages array. Place the configured basename Languages.csv or Languages.tsv in the game root, beside index.html, not data/. CSV uses semicolons; TSV uses tabs. UTF-8 header starts Key followed by language column names such as English and Portuguese. Each row must have the same number of cells; keys and column names must be nonempty and unique after case/whitespace normalization. Use
inside cells instead of physical newlines. Example CSV: Key;English;Portuguese followed by a new row Greeting;Hello;Ola. Author Show Text as $[Greeting] or \KEY[Greeting]. Key lookup ignores case/outer whitespace, but language-column lookup uses the exact configured locale spelling after trimming the header. A missing key returns undefined (explicit replacement can render "undefined"); a missing/empty language cell renders UNDEFINED!, not an English fallback. HTTP/parse failure stops database readiness with a load error; no file is created by the runtime. See MSG-BEH-language-write-boundary for CLI create/convert/validate commands.
entries.expected: Localization table format, file basenames, language list and default locale are configured by the named fields of this structure.

Empty/unconfigured language family uses rmmz-mainfont; the Database advanced fallbackFonts list is appended to the chosen family for unavailable glyphs/browser font fallback. entries.title: plugin/LanguageImages:struct
entries.context: Requires localization enabled. ImageManager.loadBitmap replaces the exact uppercase marker [XX] in its filename argument (which may include subfolders), not in its separate folder argument. It substitutes the selected language string when ConvertDefault=true or the current locale differs from DefaultLocale. Example: show picture "Title_[XX]", set /LanguageImages/Portuguese="pt", and select Portuguese; img/pictures/Title_pt.png must exist. A marker in a filename subpath such as "[XX]/Title" resolves img/pictures/pt/Title.png. Empty/missing mapping leaves [XX] unchanged. There is no automatic fallback to the default-language asset if a resolved file is missing; normal image-load failure applies. Install all required assets. This does not translate image pixels or generate files.

entries.context: Player text speed uses 1..10 from slowest to fastest; 11 is Instant. entries.title: struct:AutoColor/TextColor1:arraystr
entries.context: Enable Coreto_0_CoreEngine then Coreto_1_MessageCore. Configure /AutoColor/TextColor1 as a JSON array of strings, for example ["Potion"], using message parameters set with --project selecting the MZ game. Reload the editor/restart after editing. Message, Help, ChoiceList and an available TextPopup use automatic coloring. Latin entries match case-sensitively at word boundaries, globally; entries containing recognized CJK/symbol characters match a case-insensitive literal occurrence without word boundaries and without the global flag. Empty/numeric-only entries are ignored. Rules compile by ascending palette index and descending word length inside each color, and run sequentially; overlapping entries can therefore wrap earlier replacements, so keep a word in one color list for predictable output. Database-name rules join these lists; live actor-name coloring runs afterwards. COLORLOCK blocks drawing-time color changes. Existing palette cells come from img/system/Window.png; this field does not change the RGB colors. See message api describe MSG-BEH-autocolor --json for the full pipeline.
entries.expected: Eligible matches from this list select palette index 1, subject to matching, ordering and color-lock rules. Empty/numeric entries are ignored; other lists, database categories and actor rules can also color text.

Configure /AutoColor/TextColor17 as a JSON array of strings, for example ["Potion"], using message parameters set with --project selecting the MZ game. Reload the editor/restart after editing. Message, Help, ChoiceList and an available TextPopup use automatic coloring. Latin entries match case-sensitively at word boundaries, globally; entries containing recognized CJK/symbol characters match a case-insensitive literal occurrence without word boundaries and without the global flag. Empty/numeric-only entries are ignored. Rules compile by ascending palette index and descending word length inside each color, and run sequentially; overlapping entries can therefore wrap earlier replacements, so keep a word in one color list for predictable output. Database-name rules join these lists; live actor-name coloring runs afterwards. COLORLOCK blocks drawing-time color changes. Existing palette cells come from img/system/Window.png; this field does not change the RGB colors. See message api describe MSG-BEH-autocolor --json for the full pipeline.
entries.expected: Eligible matches from this list select palette index 17, subject to matching, ordering and color-lock rules. Empty/numeric entries are ignored; other lists, database categories and actor rules can also color text.
entries.availabilityReason: Ative o plugin indicado e suas dependências no jogo. Disponibilidade descreve a capacidade, não verifica a configuração do projeto.

ActionJS is a function body with this=the text window and arguments[0]=textState (text,index,x,y,startX,startY,drawing,buffer among its fields). It runs during drawing and measurement; guard side effects with state.drawing. CommonEvent runs only during real Window_Message drawing on a map, not measurement or battle, requires an existing event ID, and starts a separate map-updated interpreter without blocking the message. Multiple triggers can overlap; map initialization/setupEvents clears them and completion removes finished interpreters; loading preserves a serialized array and initializes it only if absent. Zero disables the event.

For a string use \MARK<hello> and this.obtainEscapeString(state), which consumes the angle-bracket string and returns empty if absent. Action Type does not append its regex to the conversion matcher. ActionJS is a function body with this=the text window and arguments[0]=textState (text,index,x,y,startX,startY,drawing,buffer among its fields). It runs during drawing and measurement; guard side effects with state.drawing. CommonEvent runs only during real Window_Message drawing on a map, not measurement or battle, requires an existing event ID, and starts a separate map-updated interpreter without blocking the message. Multiple triggers can overlap; map initialization/setupEvents clears them and completion removes finished interpreters; loading preserves a serialized array and initializes it only if absent. Zero disables the event.

entries.title: struct:Localization/Enable:eval
entries.context:
Requires /Localization/Enable=true and a nonempty Languages array. Place the configured basename Languages.csv or Languages.tsv in the game root, beside index.html, not data/. CSV uses semicolons; TSV uses tabs. UTF-8 header starts Key followed by language column names such as English and Portuguese. Each row must have the same number of cells; keys and column names must be nonempty and unique after case/whitespace normalization. Use
inside cells instead of physical newlines. Example CSV: Key;English;Portuguese followed by a new row Greeting;Hello;Ola. Author Show Text as $[Greeting] or \KEY[Greeting]. Key lookup ignores case/outer whitespace, but language-column lookup uses the exact configured locale spelling after trimming the header. A missing key returns undefined (explicit replacement can render "undefined"); a missing/empty language cell renders UNDEFINED!, not an English fallback. HTTP/parse failure stops database readiness with a load error; no file is created by the runtime. See MSG-BEH-language-write-boundary for CLI create/convert/validate commands.

entries.title: struct:Localization/DefaultLocale:str
entries.context:
Requires /Localization/Enable=true and a nonempty Languages array. Place the configured basename Languages.csv or Languages.tsv in the game root, beside index.html, not data/. CSV uses semicolons; TSV uses tabs. UTF-8 header starts Key followed by language column names such as English and Portuguese. Each row must have the same number of cells; keys and column names must be nonempty and unique after case/whitespace normalization. Use
inside cells instead of physical newlines. Example CSV: Key;English;Portuguese followed by a new row Greeting;Hello;Ola. Author Show Text as $[Greeting] or \KEY[Greeting]. Key lookup ignores case/outer whitespace, but language-column lookup uses the exact configured locale spelling after trimming the header. A missing key returns undefined (explicit replacement can render "undefined"); a missing/empty language cell renders UNDEFINED!, not an English fallback. HTTP/parse failure stops database readiness with a load error; no file is created by the runtime. See MSG-BEH-language-write-boundary for CLI create/convert/validate commands.

entries.title: struct:LanguageImages/ConvertDefault:eval
entries.context: Requires localization enabled. ImageManager.loadBitmap replaces the exact uppercase marker [XX] in its filename argument (which may include subfolders), not in its separate folder argument. It substitutes the selected language string when ConvertDefault=true or the current locale differs from DefaultLocale. Example: show picture "Title_[XX]", set /LanguageImages/Portuguese="pt", and select Portuguese; img/pictures/Title_pt.png must exist. A marker in a filename subpath such as "[XX]/Title" resolves img/pictures/pt/Title.png. Empty/missing mapping leaves [XX] unchanged. There is no automatic fallback to the default-language asset if a resolved file is missing; normal image-load failure applies. Install all required assets. This does not translate image pixels or generate files.

MessageLogMenu_RectJS runs during scene window creation with this=Scene_MessageLog, no arguments, and must return a Rectangle in screen pixels; this.mainAreaTop()/mainAreaHeight() and Graphics.boxWidth are available. entries.title: MsgSoundChangeMessageSound
entries.context: Requires the external MsgLetterSounds provider identified by this entry plugin/version after its Message dependency, with message sounds enabled. Boot defaults are edited in the MZ Plugin Manager; current game settings use its Plugin Commands and are saved with game-system state. Options msgLetterSound can additionally suppress playback when that option is defined. This is editor integration, not a Coreto CLI write endpoint. Add an MZ event Plugin Command, select MsgLetterSounds → MsgSoundChangeMessageSound, and fill all eight arguments. The sound file must exist in audio/se without an extension in name:str. Volume and pitch are percentages; pan is -100..100. Variance uses percentage points/pan points, not a percent of the base. Interval is the character counter between eligible playbacks.

desc: Interval the sound effect from being played between how many characters?

entries.description: Nonnegative integer count of message text-flush attempts to skip after a sound. After an eligible playback, the counter is loaded with Interval. Each later sound-gate check decrements it and suppresses playback while the old value is greater than zero; 0 allows each otherwise eligible attempt. This is not milliseconds or update frames, and fast text can flush multiple characters together. Blacklist/enabled/Options gates still apply. Changing the setting does not reset the existing counter; a new page resets that counter to zero.

desc: Interval the sound effect from being played between how many characters?

entries.description: Nonnegative integer count of message text-flush attempts to skip after a sound. After an eligible playback, the counter is loaded with Interval. Each later sound-gate check decrements it and suppresses playback while the old value is greater than zero; 0 allows each otherwise eligible attempt. This is not milliseconds or update frames, and fast text can flush multiple characters together. Blacklist/enabled/Options gates still apply. Changing the setting does not reset the existing counter; a new page resets that counter to zero.

entries.title: plugin/Tooltip:struct
entries.context: Requires the external StateTooltips provider identified by this entry plugin/version and its dependencies. Edit its Tooltip or Vocab structure in the MZ Plugin Manager and restart the game. This is editor integration, not a Coreto CLI write endpoint. Offsets are screen pixels, positive X right and positive Y down; negative reverses direction. Hover starts at TouchInput coordinates plus OffsetX/OffsetY, optionally centered horizontally, then rounds/clamps the scaled window to screen bounds. Keyboard selection starts at the selected battler sprite x/y; front-view actors instead use status-window y minus scaled tooltip height, add status-window x and the actor-front-view offsets. It then adds screen-versus-box margins, optional horizontal centering and SelectShowOffsetX/Y. Enemy WeaknessDisplay offsets apply only when that external provider is active. Finally hover offsets also apply and the position is clamped. Keyboard selection requires SelectShowEnabled and unchanged target/mouse during SelectShowDelay milliseconds.

entries.title: struct:Tooltip/OffsetX:num
entries.context: Requires the external StateTooltips provider identified by this entry plugin/version and its dependencies. Edit its Tooltip or Vocab structure in the MZ Plugin Manager and restart the game. This is editor integration, not a Coreto CLI write endpoint. Edit Tooltip → OffsetX:num. Offsets are screen pixels, positive X right and positive Y down; negative reverses direction. Hover starts at TouchInput coordinates plus OffsetX/OffsetY, optionally centered horizontally, then rounds/clamps the scaled window to screen bounds. Keyboard selection starts at the selected battler sprite x/y; front-view actors instead use status-window y minus scaled tooltip height, add status-window x and the actor-front-view offsets. It then adds screen-versus-box margins, optional horizontal centering and SelectShowOffsetX/Y. Enemy WeaknessDisplay offsets apply only when that external provider is active. entries.title: /<CONTINUE>/gi
entries.context: Requires the Message Log provider identified by plugin/version and its Message dependency. This is automatic history normalization, not a CLI command. If an MZ Show Text body contains <CONTINUE>, this history matcher strips it; the tag is not needed to record ordinary text. Each command101 starts a new pending history entry; lines added during the same command accumulate with newlines. This tag does not join separately executed commands. A Message provider may independently combine adjacent Show Text commands into one execution; see message api describe MSG-BEH-sequencia-texto --json. A nonempty remaining body becomes a new entry, including the first entry of an empty history. An empty body, global BypassMessageLogging=true or a <BYPASS MESSAGE LOG> marker discards the pending entry. This rule describes recording only; it does not implement the live-message meaning of CONTINUE.

entries.title: /\$(?:\[|\<|\{)(.*?)(?:\]|\>|\})/gi
entries.context: Enable Coreto_0_CoreEngine then Coreto_1_MessageCore. Enter the shown text in the MZ event field specified below, using one authored backslash for escape codes. This is text authoring, not a CLI operation. The regex title describes a pipeline match; authors do not enter an ESC control character. Requires /Localization/Enable=true and at least one language in /Localization/Languages. Configure /Localization/LangFiletype as csv or tsv, the matching CsvFilename/TsvFilename basename at the game root, and DefaultLocale as a language header. UTF-8 CSV uses semicolons; TSV uses tabs. First header is Key, followed by language names; rows are rectangular with unique nonempty keys. Keys are trimmed/lowercased, while the current ConfigManager.textLocale selects the matching header (English only when that value is empty). Missing key inserts undefined; an empty/missing cell inserts UNDEFINED!; there is no automatic fallback translation. Use MSG-BEH-language-write-boundary for table creation/conversion/validation commands. Opening [, < or { and closing ], > or } are accepted by this matcher, including mixed pairs; use matching delimiters for readable authored text. The dollar form has no leading backslash.
entries.expected: With English selected, displays Hello from the Greeting row.

Enter the tag in an option text field of the MZ Show Choices event command. It is removed from the visible label; the remaining text names the choice. Only without either bare gate do the switch conditions run; multiple distinct switch gates can then reject the item. Prefer one explicit gate per item. Visibility accepts SW, SWITCH or SWITCHES, while enablement accepts SWITCH/SWITCHES only. Names such as lowerleft, center and upperright are accepted. An unpositioned BG tag makes foreground placement use the unpositioned layout too. Resources load asynchronously and obsolete item/layout requests are ignored. Use exactly the colon/space syntax shown in the example. IMG, IMAGE, PIC and PICTURE are supported names. For anchored tags, the no-space spelling FGIMAGE/BGIMAGE is also removed correctly by display cleanup.

This is text authoring, not a CLI operation. The regex title describes a pipeline match; authors do not enter an ESC control character. entries.title: /<POSITION:[ ](\d+)>/gi
entries.context: Enable Coreto_0_CoreEngine then Coreto_1_MessageCore. Enter the shown text in the MZ event field specified below, using one authored backslash for escape codes. This is text authoring, not a CLI operation. The regex title describes a pipeline match; authors do not enter an ESC control character. Use a nonnegative integer n: 0 left, 5 center, 10 right are the usual positions. Values above 10 are also accepted; geometric clamping keeps the box within the edges. entries.title: /<SHOW[ ](?:|ALL )(?:SW|SWITCH|SWITCHES):[ ](.*?)>/i
entries.context: Enable Coreto_0_CoreEngine then Coreto_1_MessageCore. Enter the shown text in the MZ event field specified below, using one authored backslash for escape codes. This is text authoring, not a CLI operation. The regex title describes a pipeline match; authors do not enter an ESC control character. Enter the tag in an option text field of the MZ Show Choices event command. It is removed from the visible label; the remaining text names the choice. It does not change which branch that choice executes. Switch payload is a comma-separated list of positive game-switch IDs, for example 1,2,3, whose values are set with MZ Control Switches. Use the exact colon/space syntax in the aliases. ALL (or omitted ALL) requires every listed switch on; ANY requires at least one on. SHOW/HIDE gates control visibility; ENABLE/DISABLE gates control selection. Bare HIDE/DISABLE rejects first. Otherwise bare SHOW/ENABLE accepts immediately, bypassing every switch gate. Only without either bare gate do the switch conditions run; multiple distinct switch gates can then reject the item. Prefer one explicit gate per item. Visibility accepts SW, SWITCH or SWITCHES, while enablement accepts SWITCH/SWITCHES only. Visibilidade/habilitação seguem gates: HIDE/DISABLE explícitos têm precedência; ALL exige todos switches ON, ANY exige ao menos um; índices originais são preservados. SW só é aceito onde o regex de visibilidade o reconhece, não como alias de habilitação.

entries.context: Enable Coreto_0_CoreEngine then Coreto_1_MessageCore. Enter the shown text in the MZ event field specified below, using one authored backslash for escape codes. Enter the tag in an option text field of the MZ Show Choices event command. It is removed from the visible label; the remaining text names the choice. It does not change which branch that choice executes. Use an existing image basename from img/pictures without .png. Portrait is an illustrative name requiring img/pictures/Portrait.png. BG is drawn behind the cursor/text; FG draws on the foreground contents and the label is drawn above it. Without an anchor the bitmap stretches to the item rectangle inset by 2 pixels. With an anchor it preserves aspect ratio; BG may enlarge, whereas FG is capped at its original size. Anchors 1..9 use keypad positions: 1 lower-left, 2 lower-center, 3 lower-right, 4 middle-left, 5 center, 6 middle-right, 7 upper-left, 8 upper-center, 9 upper-right. Names such as lowerleft, center and upperright are accepted. An unpositioned BG tag makes foreground placement use the unpositioned layout too. Resources load asynchronously and obsolete item/layout requests are ignored. Use exactly the colon/space syntax shown in the example. IMG, IMAGE, PIC and PICTURE are supported names. For anchored tags, the no-space spelling FGIMAGE/BGIMAGE is also removed correctly by display cleanup.

entries.title: TextCodeReplace/ActorFace
entries.context: Enable Coreto_0_CoreEngine then Coreto_1_MessageCore. Use the example in an MZ Show Text event text field, with one authored backslash plus its token/argument. The shipped row must still exist in the effective /TextCodeReplace configuration; its full original fields/function body are shown in default. IDs, names and icon indices in the example are illustrative and must correspond to the current project/state. The description specifies which database or party/troop domain supplies the value; a numeric database ID is not a party position unless explicitly stated. This conversion does not execute an offline CLI capability. Resolve $gameActors.actor(n), ID de ator do banco; somente quando this.constructor === Window_Message e ator existe, atribui faceName/faceIndex ao Game_Message. Sempre substitui código por string vazia; não emite nome nem ícone. É conversão prévia, não ChangeFace durante desenho. TextStr wins if nonempty and not Undefined; otherwise TextJS executes as a function body with this=the text window and String.replace match/capture/offset/source arguments. Rules are longest Match first and variables expand after each rule. Face replacement is restricted to Window_Message; ordinary name/value replacements also work in other formatted-text windows using this pipeline.

entries.description: \LETTERSOUNDINTERVAL[n] changes the message-sound interval. Nonnegative integer count of message text-flush attempts to skip after a sound. After an eligible playback, the counter is loaded with Interval. Each later sound-gate check decrements it and suppresses playback while the old value is greater than zero; 0 allows each otherwise eligible attempt. This is not milliseconds or update frames, and fast text can flush multiple characters together. Blacklist/enabled/Options gates still apply. Changing the setting does not reset the existing counter; a new page resets that counter to zero.

Text escapes change game-system state during drawing and persist across message pages and game saves until changed again. A new page resets only the letter interval counter, not these settings. The provider MsgSoundResetMessageSound command restores sound parameters but preserves the current enabled flag. New game initializes defaults. Options msgLetterSound=false still suppresses playback. Nonnegative integer variation in pan points. For V>0, the random offset is an integer from -V through V-1 and is added to base pan without a provider clamp. Zero disables variation. V=5 gives offsets -5..4; choose base pan and variation to stay within -100..100. This escape consumes bracketed nonnegative decimal integers. For negative base pan, use the provider plugin parameter or MsgSoundChangeMessageSound pan:num argument instead.

entries.title: autocolor
entries.context: Requires Coreto_0_CoreEngine followed by Coreto_1_MessageCore. Use the MZ event editor for event commands and text; configure plugin defaults through the Coreto parameter authoring interface. Illustrative variable/event/asset IDs must exist in the project. Configure /AutoColor/TextColor1 through TextColor31 as arrays of words; TextColor0 does not generate compiled rules. Example TextColor2=["Potion"]. Message, Help, ChoiceList and an available TextPopup opt in; other windows do not by default. Non-actor database categories collect valid names during database parsing when their configured category color is positive; icon escapes are removed from the matching name. Rules compile lazily when dirty, by ascending color and descending word length inside each color. Latin rules use case-sensitive global word boundaries. Words containing recognized CJK/symbol characters use a case-insensitive non-global literal match without word boundaries. Live actor names are processed afterwards with Latin-style boundaries; renaming actors updates that live path, not already collected names from other categories. Empty/numeric names are skipped; database names also exclude reserved escape names and separator names. COLORLOCK blocks actual color changes.

Requires Coreto_0_CoreEngine followed by Coreto_1_MessageCore. Use the MZ event editor for event commands and text; configure plugin defaults through the Coreto parameter authoring interface. Illustrative variable/event/asset IDs must exist in the project. Set /Localization/Enable=true, Languages=["English"], LangFiletype="csv", CsvFilename="Languages.csv", DefaultLocale="English". Put UTF-8 Languages.csv at the game root with exactly two lines: Key;English then Greeting;Hello. Each row must match the header width; the minimal valid table does not require the template full language set. Column names/keys cannot be empty or duplicate after trim/lowercase normalization. CSV delimiter is semicolon; TSV delimiter is tab. Quoted cells may contain the delimiter, and doubled quotes represent a quote; quotes must enclose the whole cell. Physical newlines inside cells are rejected: use
. LF/CRLF accepted, bare CR rejected, initial BOM removed. Current textLocale selects a case-sensitive language header; keys normalize to lowercase/trim. Missing key produces undefined, missing/empty selected cell UNDEFINED!, with no translation fallback.
entries.expected: Parser usa ; no CSV e tab no TSV, chaves trim/lowercase, colunas por locale; preserva regra de quotes da fonte.
entries.availabilityReason: Ative o plugin indicado e suas dependências no jogo. Disponibilidade descreve a capacidade, não verifica a configuração do projeto.

entries.title: idioma-authoring
entries.context:
Requires Coreto_0_CoreEngine followed by Coreto_1_MessageCore. Use the MZ event editor for event commands and text; configure plugin defaults through the Coreto parameter authoring interface. Illustrative variable/event/asset IDs must exist in the project. Execute a CLI com --project apontando para o jogo MZ. Nomes devem ser basenames com extensão .csv ou .tsv, sem subpastas; o destino de create/convert não pode existir. CSV usa ponto e vírgula, TSV usa tabulação, ambos em UTF-8. A primeira coluna deve ser Key e as seguintes nomes de idiomas, sem nomes ou chaves vazias/duplicadas; todas as linhas devem ter a mesma quantidade de células. Use
em vez de quebras físicas dentro de células. --format e --name explícitos evitam depender dos nomes configurados em Localization. Depois de criar ou converter, configure Localization.Enable, LangFiletype e CsvFilename/TsvFilename para carregar a tabela no jogo; a CLI não ativa essa configuração automaticamente. The create template contains Key plus 28 named languages (29 columns); a hand-authored table needs only Key plus the languages it actually provides. Use message api describe MSG-BEH-language-write-boundary --json for the three concrete operations.
entries.expected: Gera somente template original Key+28 idiomas e Greeting/Farewell/Wow; CSV→TSV preserva contrato explícito de conversão.
entries.availabilityReason: Ative o plugin indicado e suas dependências no jogo. Disponibilidade descreve a capacidade, não verifica a configuração do projeto.

entries.title: boot-falha-recuperacao
entries.context:
Requires Coreto_0_CoreEngine followed by Coreto_1_MessageCore. Use the MZ event editor for event commands and text; configure plugin defaults through the Coreto parameter authoring interface. Illustrative variable/event/asset IDs must exist in the project. Set /Localization/Enable=true, Languages=["English"], LangFiletype="csv", CsvFilename="Languages.csv", DefaultLocale="English". Put UTF-8 Languages.csv at the game root with exactly two lines: Key;English then Greeting;Hello. Each row must match the header width; the minimal valid table does not require the template full language set. Column names/keys cannot be empty or duplicate after trim/lowercase normalization. CSV delimiter is semicolon; TSV delimiter is tab. Quoted cells may contain the delimiter, and doubled quotes represent a quote; quotes must enclose the whole cell. Physical newlines inside cells are rejected: use
. LF/CRLF accepted, bare CR rejected, initial BOM removed. Current textLocale selects a case-sensitive language header; keys normalize to lowercase/trim. Missing key produces undefined, missing/empty selected cell UNDEFINED!, with no translation fallback. Serve the game through its normal HTTP/NW.js runtime. Enabled localization with a nonempty Languages list loads the configured root basename. HTTP success accepts status 200..399, parses before marking ready, and boot waits for ready. Network, timeout (30000ms), bad HTTP status or malformed table enter an error state; isDatabaseLoaded exposes LoadError with filename/reason and a retry callback. Correct the file/configuration/server first, then use the error-screen retry; a replacement request aborts the prior pending request and stale completions are ignored. Runtime never creates, converts or overwrites language files. CLI validation is available via message api describe MSG-BEH-language-write-boundary --json.

entries.title: selecao-lifecycle
entries.context: Enable Coreto_0_CoreEngine, Coreto_1_MessageCore and Coreto_3_ChoiceCmnEvts in dependency order. In a Show Choices option label use <CHOICE COMMON EVENT: 3>Preview. ID 3 is a positive database Common Event ID and must exist. The six accepted forms combine CHOICE or SELECT with COMMON EVENT, COMMONEVENT or EVENT, with a space after the colon. Tags are removed from the visible label. A changed selection starts the selected row event without confirming that choice or waiting for the Common Event; staying on the same row does not retrigger. Starting a choice window deselects first, so its initial selection can trigger. Multiple tags on one label leave the last ID; separate changes can launch overlapping map interpreters. Map initialization/setupEvents clears those interpreters; completed ones are removed. Load preserves a serialized array and initializes it only if absent. Normal supported context is Scene_Map. Battle/other scenes do not launch the event and issue one alert per game-temp lifetime. The explicit EventedTitleMap exception is described by message api describe CCE-BEH-evented-title-map --json. Runtime maps row indices after the choice list is built, so authored branches remain independent from preview events.
entries.expected: CE inicia por mudança de seleção reconhecida; remove tag do label visível e aplica trim; não bloqueia interpretador pai.
entries.availabilityReason: Ative o plugin indicado e suas dependências no jogo. Disponibilidade descreve a capacidade, não verifica a configuração do projeto.

entries.title: registro-captura
entries.context: Requires the external Message Log provider identified by this entry plugin/version, enabled after its Message dependency. This is MZ editor/runtime integration, not a Coreto CLI capability execution. Edit provider Plugin Manager parameters for boot defaults; its Plugin Commands change saved game-system flags. Set General/EntryLimit to a positive maximum entry count. BypassMessageLogging with Bypass:eval="false" permits capture; true bypasses it. Show Text containing <BYPASS MESSAGE LOG> is also excluded. Each Show Text command creates an entry, converts text/macros/variables/replacements for capture, and stores face filename/index plus converted speaker. Empty or immediately identical serialized entries are omitted; adding beyond EntryLimit removes oldest entries. The Show Text wrapper sets a temporary capture flag, including for event Show Text in battle; other direct battle additions are skipped without that flag. Choice/number/item input recording has a separate map-scene gate. Native action/wait/window/CE codes are stripped according to the published LOG-RX entries, not executed by history display. EntryLimit=0 retains no entries; do not use negative limits.
entries.expected: Registro congela valores mostrados de variáveis/macros/substituições, falante e face, preservando limites de entradas.
entries.availabilityReason: Ative o plugin indicado e suas dependências no jogo. Disponibilidade descreve a capacidade, não verifica a configuração do projeto.

entries.title: entradas-input
entries.context: Requires the external Message Log provider identified by this entry plugin/version, enabled after its Message dependency. This is MZ editor/runtime integration, not a Coreto CLI capability execution. Edit provider Plugin Manager parameters for boot defaults; its Plugin Commands change saved game-system flags. The hooks require the actual map scene while SCENE_MAP_ONLY is true. Vocab/ChoiceFmt substitutes %1 with the selected authored choice; cancel-to-choice uses that choice, while a dedicated cancel branch uses Vocab/ChoiceCancel. Vocab/NumberFmt substitutes %1 with the confirmed number. Vocab/ItemNameFmt substitutes %1 with an icon escape and %2 with item name; Vocab/ItemFmt receives that formatted name as %1, or Vocab/NoItem for cancel/no item. Window/ColorLockChoice, ColorLockNumber and ColorLockItem wrap the substituted value in color-lock tags. These affect presentation only, not the chosen branch/value. Capture still respects bypass, deduplication and EntryLimit. There is no separate input-capture enable flag in this contract.

entries.title: navegacao-scene
entries.context: Requires the external Message Log provider identified by this entry plugin/version, enabled after its Message dependency. This is MZ editor/runtime integration, not a Coreto CLI capability execution. Edit provider Plugin Manager parameters for boot defaults; its Plugin Commands change saved game-system flags. Set MainMenu/ShowMainMenu=true and EnableMainMenu=true, then capture at least one entry; empty history disables access. Name is the menu label. The SystemShowMessageLogMenu and SystemEnableMessageLogMenu commands change these flags separately. General/ShortcutKey is an MZ input symbol (for example pageup): while a map message is at its input check, a triggered shortcut opens history if the enabled/history gate passes; the visibility flag only controls the menu row. In history, up/down scroll slowly, pageup/pagedown quickly, home/end jump top/bottom and cancel returns. The held opening hotkey must be released before it scrolls. Window scroll speeds are pixels per update; sound-frequency fields are update-frame divisors. The native menu route is inserted automatically when no Main Menu Core provider is active. Extended Message can separately expose a backlog/log button; consult ext-message api describe EXT-M-122 --json for the wheel route and its independent gates. These routes all push the history scene; opening preloads stored faces.
entries.expected: Abertura respeita busy/visibilidade/habilitação; voltar restaura mensagem e scroll sem efeito de gameplay.
entries.availabilityReason: Ative o plugin indicado e suas dependências no jogo. Disponibilidade descreve a capacidade, não verifica a configuração do projeto.

entries.title: gate-blacklist
entries.context: Enable the external Message Letter Sounds provider identified by this entry after its Message dependency. Configure an existing audio/se basename and its SE fields in Plugin Manager, then SystemEnableMessageSounds with Enable:eval="true" (or Show Text \LSON). OFF forms disable saved state until reenabled; new pages do not reenable. If the compatible Options integration defines msgLetterSound=false it suppresses playback first. The interval counter then decrements and suppresses while its old value is positive; saved enable and real drawing are also required. Empty buffer, a single space, newline/carriage return, a buffer matching bracketed [...] or angle <...> text, or an exact member of BlackList are rejected. BlackList is an array of exact text-buffer strings, not a regex or substring list. Fast text may combine characters into one buffer. Accepted playback loads the interval setting; a new page resets only the counter. Volume/pitch/pan variances and persistent setting escapes are documented in message api describe SND-M-001 --json and SND-ESC-005.
entries.expected: Som de letra depende de toggle jogo, toggle jogador, drawing, intervalo e blacklist.
entries.availabilityReason: Ative o plugin indicado e suas dependências no jogo. Disponibilidade descreve a capacidade, não verifica a configuração do projeto.

entries.context: Enable the State Tooltips provider identified by this entry plugin/version after its Battle, Message and Skills/States dependencies. Use exactly one Message implementation. Edit State Tooltips in the MZ Plugin Manager (Tooltip, Vocab and Window structures), then restart the game. This is editor integration; no Coreto command writes these external parameters or executes a tooltip. The battler must be alive, appeared and have presentable content; an empty tooltip stays hidden. Author a state in Database → States with a nonempty name, iconIndex greater than zero and Notes. <State Tooltip Description>...</State Tooltip Description> supplies the specific description; otherwise <Help Description>...</Help Description>, then Vocab/HelpDescription:json (default "-") is used. An empty specific description falls back to the general description. A name containing -----, a truthy excludeListing flag, or <EXCLUDE FROM TOOLTIP>/<EXCLUDE FROM TOOLTIPS> in Notes omits the line without removing the mechanical state. The tooltip keeps the order returned by battler.states(); it does not promise application order. Vocab/StateFmt:str placeholders are %1 icon escape, %2 name, %3 description, %4 duration, %5 state color. Inside the state description itself, %1 instead receives getStateDisplay(state.id), usually empty when no custom display exists. Timing 0 has no duration text, even for passive states. For timed removal, a passiveStates() member uses PassiveText; timing 1 uses ActionsFmt, other timings TurnsFmt, with %1=stateTurns(id)||0 and %2=color. Empty templates may hide a line. To inspect, set Window/Window_MenuStatus:eval=true, give a living actor the described effect, open the menu and hover its actor row. For enemy/battle target selection, use message api describe TIP-BEH-interacao --json.
entries.expected: Estados são exibidos por ordem do battler e com descrição específica/fallback; filtros removem só a apresentação.
entries.availabilityReason: Ative o plugin indicado e suas dependências no jogo. Disponibilidade descreve a capacidade, não verifica a configuração do projeto.

entries.title: buffs
entries.context: Enable the State Tooltips provider identified by this entry plugin/version after its Battle, Message and Skills/States dependencies. Use exactly one Message implementation. Edit State Tooltips in the MZ Plugin Manager (Tooltip, Vocab and Window structures), then restart the game. This is editor integration; no Coreto command writes these external parameters or executes a tooltip. The battler must be alive, appeared and have presentable content; an empty tooltip stays hidden. Create actual buffs/debuffs in Database → Skills or Items → Effects → Add Buff/Add Debuff, choosing a parameter and duration in turns. Parameter IDs are 0 Max HP, 1 Max MP, 2 ATK, 3 DEF, 4 MAT, 5 MDF, 6 AGI, 7 LUK; names use game database terms. Vocab/BuffFmt:str or DebuffFmt:str uses %1 icon escape, %2 parameter name, %3 floor(paramBuffRate(id)*100), %4 duration, %5 buff/debuff color. The percentage is the final multiplier (125 means 125%, not +125). TurnsFmt receives %1=buffTurns(id), %2=color, including zero. Level zero has no line. Skills/States Buffs/StackBuffMax, StackDebuffMax and MultiplierJS own stack limits and rate; defaults are two levels and max(0,1+level*0.25). The tooltip does not impose those limits. Only the displayed buff icon clamps levels to -2..2; rates may differ with custom rules. Colors come from Skills/States Buffs/ColorBuff and ColorDebuff. Empty templates hide text, not the effect. To inspect, set Window/Window_MenuStatus:eval=true, give a living actor the described effect, open the menu and hover its actor row. For enemy/battle target selection, use message api describe TIP-BEH-interacao --json.
entries.expected: Buff/debuff exibe ícone, nome do parâmetro, floor(rate*100), turnos e cor correspondentes.
entries.availabilityReason: Ative o plugin indicado e suas dependências no jogo. Disponibilidade descreve a capacidade, não verifica a configuração do projeto.

examples.input: Give an ally-targeting support skill Effect → Add Buff → Attack → 3 turns. Set Vocab/BuffFmt:str="%2: %3% %4" and TurnsFmt:str="(%1 turnos)". Apply it once and inspect the actor before expiry.
examples.expected: With default rate rules, one positive level displays 125%; duration shows the remaining actual counter rather than always the originally authored 3 turns.

entries.title: interacao
entries.context: Enable the State Tooltips provider identified by this entry plugin/version after its Battle, Message and Skills/States dependencies. Use exactly one Message implementation. Edit State Tooltips in the MZ Plugin Manager (Tooltip, Vocab and Window structures), then restart the game. This is editor integration; no Coreto command writes these external parameters or executes a tooltip. The battler must be alive, appeared and have presentable content; an empty tooltip stays hidden. Window flags use exact constructor names: Window_MenuStatus, Window_MenuActor, Window_SkillStatus, Window_EquipStatus, Window_Status and Window_BattleStatus (all :eval fields in Window). MenuStatus/BattleStatus resolve the actor at the hovered row; SkillStatus/EquipStatus/Status use the whole rectangle and their current actor. Hover requires an enabled, open, visible window and pointer in its region, not confirmation or an active flag. Parent transforms/scroll are considered. Leaving/closing the region closes only its owned tooltip. Battler sprite hover uses mouse-enter; do not assume touch-only input generates sprite hover. Keyboard-selected tooltips temporarily suspend window hover. Tooltip/SelectShowEnabled:eval=true and SelectShowDelay:num=1500 enable delayed target lookup in milliseconds. A recent left/right/up/down/ok input in an active battle target window schedules it; a programmatic index change alone is insufficient. Target and pointer must remain unchanged, with the same live scene/window and living appeared battler; a sprite must resolve. New selection, pointer movement, leaving both target windows, scene termination or destruction cancels/closes it. Dead battlers close their tooltip. Tooltip/Scale:num=0.6 is the size ratio (1 normal); use a positive value. WindowSkin:str is an img/system basename without .png, WindowOpacity:num is 0..255. OffsetX/Y are common pixels, positive right/down; BaseShowCenter centers horizontally for hover. Keyboard selection starts at the battler sprite, applies box margins/SelectShowCenter and SelectShowOffsetX/Y, native frontview actor offsets, optional enemy offsets, then common offsets and screen clamps. Clamps use scaled dimensions; oversized content is not paginated. In battle, an open active actor-command/item/skill/choice window under the pointer suppresses tooltip opacity.
entries.expected: Hover/touch/target seleciona battler correto; tooltip respeita cobertura, clamp, morte e movimento do ponteiro.
entries.availabilityReason: Ative o plugin indicado e suas dependências no jogo. Disponibilidade descreve a capacidade, não verifica a configuração do projeto.

examples.input: Enable Window/Window_MenuStatus:eval=true and hover a living actor row with a visible state. For battle targets set Tooltip/SelectShowEnabled:eval=true and SelectShowDelay:num=1500; move selection with an arrow and leave target/pointer still for 1.5 seconds.
examples.expected: The eligible actor/target tooltip appears; changing target, leaving selection or moving the pointer cancels/closes the delayed view.

entries.title: choice-image-pos-1
entries.context: Enable Coreto_0_CoreEngine and Coreto_1_MessageCore. Author the tag directly in a Show Choices option text. The filename is an existing basename from img/pictures without .png; FixturePicture requires img/pictures/FixturePicture.png. BG is behind the item cursor/text and may enlarge to fit; FG is on foreground contents, preserves aspect ratio and never enlarges above original size, with text drawn over it. Anchored variants use keypad positions 1..9: bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right, middle-left, center, middle-right, top-left, top-center, top-right. Use the no-space anchored spelling FGIMAGE/BGIMAGE so cleanup removes the tag. The remaining label names the choice and its branch is unchanged.
entries.expected: Imagem ancorada na posição numpad 1; BG pode ampliar, FG limita escala a1 e redesenha texto por cima.

entries.title: dialog-save
entries.context: Requires compatible Extended Message and Save providers plus Message. Configure the console with a save button and enable/visible console state; saving must be enabled and current scene must be map. See ext-message api describe EXT-BEH-console-save --json for the console entry; the concrete route is the save button in /Buttons/List. The special save scene finds the deepest current map interpreter and temporarily sets its index to the last recorded Show Text index for serialization, then restores the live index after requesting save. Returning from the menu keeps the current live message; loading reconstructs from that saved command, not a snapshot of the visual character cursor, choice hover or partially typed glyphs. Use ordinary map-event Show Text for this route; a missing recorded Show Text index is not a guaranteed resume point.

entries.title: state-data
entries.context: This entry plugin/version identifies the Skills/States provider. State Tooltips is a separate provider: its exact plugin/version and dependencies are identified by message api describe TIP-BEH-filtro-state --json. Enable both providers in their required order with exactly one Message implementation. Edit State Tooltips in the MZ Plugin Manager, then restart. This is editor integration; no Coreto command writes these external parameters or executes a tooltip. The battler must be alive, appeared and have presentable content; an empty tooltip stays hidden. The external Skills/States provider owns states(), getStateDisplay(stateId), passiveStates(), stateTurns(stateId), buffTurns(paramId), paramBuffRate(paramId) and state/buff colors. These are battler runtime methods, not CLI operations or an alternative state system. StateTooltips consumes their current results. Author ordinary Database states and skill/item buff effects, then configure StateTooltips Vocab formats. A state-specific description %1 inserts getStateDisplay; state duration timing 0 is empty, timed passive uses PassiveText, timing 1 ActionsFmt, otherwise TurnsFmt. Buff formats use the final multiplier percentage and remaining turns. Use message api describe TIP-BEH-filtro-state --json and TIP-BEH-buffs --json for complete templates/gates and TIP-BEH-interacao for opening the tooltip. Coreto does not manufacture absent provider methods.
entries.expected: APIs de state display, passiveStates, stateTurns, buffTurns e cores alimentam tooltip original sem migrar sistema de estados.
entries.availabilityReason: Ative o plugin indicado e suas dependências no jogo. Disponibilidade descreve a capacidade, não verifica a configuração do projeto.

entries.title: enemy-aspects
entries.context: Enable the State Tooltips provider identified by this entry plugin/version after its Battle, Message and Skills/States dependencies. Use exactly one Message implementation. Edit State Tooltips in the MZ Plugin Manager (Tooltip, Vocab and Window structures), then restart the game. This is editor integration; no Coreto command writes these external parameters or executes a tooltip. The battler must be alive, appeared and have presentable content; an empty tooltip stays hidden. Battle provider 1.85 supplies enemy aspect authoring in Database → Enemies → Notes. Use <Aspect Name: Blindado>, <Aspect Icon: 26>, <Aspect Color: 2>, and <Aspect Description>...</Aspect Description>. Names accept %1 for the original enemy name, icon is a numeric IconSet index, color a 0..31 palette index or #rrggbb. A nonempty description is required by hasAspectData(); name/icon alone do not enable an aspect. Defaults are name "%1 Aspect", icon 26 and color 2, but description empty. State Tooltips Vocab/EnemyAspectFmt:str uses %1 icon escape, %2 name, %3 description, %4 color. Empty format hides the aspect line. This is enemy-only presentation placed before state/buff lines; it does not create armor/resistance/weakness mechanics. To inspect a living enemy use hover or keyboard selection per message api describe TIP-BEH-interacao --json.
entries.expected: Enemy com aspecto do BattleCore e formato não vazio exibe ícone/nome/descrição/cor; sem aspecto/ator/formato vazio não exibe linha.
entries.availabilityReason: Requer Battle Core 1.85 com hasAspectData/getAspectData para obter os aspectos do inimigo.

entries.title: voice-replay
entries.context: Requires the external Message Log provider identified by this entry plugin/version, enabled after its Message dependency. This is MZ editor/runtime integration, not a Coreto CLI capability execution. Edit provider Plugin Manager parameters for boot defaults; its Plugin Commands change saved game-system flags. Message Log consumes the provider-defined voice-text matcher and reads its first capture as comma-separated name,volume,pitch,pan: name defaults empty, volume/pitch default 100 and clamp 0..100 here, pan defaults 0 and clamps -100..100. entries.title: io-no-overwrite
entries.context: Run the installed CLI with --project pointing to the intended existing MZ game. Paths/IDs below are illustrative and must match existing map/event/page/command data. Use list/get to inspect before writing, pass JSON for --value and reload the editor after a write so an old editor buffer does not overwrite it. --dry-run validates/previews without writing. The CLI does not execute authored JS or the game. Existing-file edits read a regular non-symlink file inside the selected root, create a same-directory temporary file, verify the original hash/inode/device/mode before replacement and confirm the written bytes. FILE_CONFLICT means inspect/read again; WRITE_UNCONFIRMED means replacement/publication may already have happened, so inspect before retrying. Language create and CSV-to-TSV convert publish only new root basenames; LANGUAGE_FILE_EXISTS refuses an existing destination and conversion preserves its source. This guarantee is per file/operation, not a multi-command transaction. Ani preset --expected-hash is a separate API; Message edits do not accept that option.

entries.title: optional-mainmenu
entries.context: Requires the external Message Log provider identified by this entry plugin/version, enabled after its Message dependency. This is MZ editor/runtime integration, not a Coreto CLI capability execution. Edit provider Plugin Manager parameters for boot defaults; its Plugin Commands change saved game-system flags. Set MainMenu/ShowMainMenu=true and EnableMainMenu=true, then capture at least one entry; empty history disables access. Name is the menu label. The SystemShowMessageLogMenu and SystemEnableMessageLogMenu commands change these flags separately. General/ShortcutKey is an MZ input symbol (for example pageup): while a map message is at its input check, a triggered shortcut opens history if the enabled/history gate passes; the visibility flag only controls the menu row. In history, up/down scroll slowly, pageup/pagedown quickly, home/end jump top/bottom and cancel returns. The held opening hotkey must be released before it scrolls. Window scroll speeds are pixels per update; sound-frequency fields are update-frame divisors. When a compatible Main Menu Core provider is active, Message Log deliberately stops automatically inserting its row. The provider-owned command list must include a row whose symbol is messageLog; the Message Log Scene_Menu hook registers that handler to push Scene_MessageLog. Use the provider command-list editor to apply its own row schema and its visibility/enabled callbacks to the exposed Window_MenuCommand.isMessageLogCommandVisible()/isMessageLogCommandEnabled() methods. This package does not supply or configure the external menu provider. Without it, the same row is inserted automatically according to Message Log flags. Runtime helper calls must run on a real Window_MenuCommand instance, not a CLI shell.
entries.expected: Com MainMenuCore ativo, usa sua integração de menu. Sem ele, usa o menu nativo e a configuração automática.
entries.availabilityReason: Com MainMenuCore ativo, usa sua integração de menu. Sem ele, usa o menu nativo e a configuração automática.

entries.title: Exceção de cena EventedTitleMap
entries.context: Enable Coreto_0_CoreEngine, Coreto_1_MessageCore and Coreto_3_ChoiceCmnEvts in dependency order. In a Show Choices option label use <CHOICE COMMON EVENT: 3>Preview. ID 3 is a positive database Common Event ID and must exist. The six accepted forms combine CHOICE or SELECT with COMMON EVENT, COMMONEVENT or EVENT, with a space after the colon. Tags are removed from the visible label. A changed selection starts the selected row event without confirming that choice or waiting for the Common Event; staying on the same row does not retrigger. Starting a choice window deselects first, so its initial selection can trigger. Multiple tags on one label leave the last ID; separate changes can launch overlapping map interpreters. Map initialization/setupEvents clears those interpreters; completed ones are removed. Load preserves a serialized array and initializes it only if absent. Besides instances of Scene_Map, the adapter accepts a current scene whose constructor.name is exactly Scene_EventedTitleMap. The external provider must create that real scene and supply functioning map/message/choice/interpreter lifecycle, including $gameMap.addMessageCommonEvent and updates. Merely setting an Imported flag or naming an unrelated class does not supply those facilities. Configure the external provider own title-map setup before placing the same Show Choices event on that map; this package does not install that provider or define its configuration schema. Coreto Event Title Scene is not an automatic alias for this exact class contract. Without the external scene, author this feature on an ordinary map.
entries.expected: isSceneSelectChoiceCommonEventValid aceita Scene_Map ou constructor.name Scene_EventedTitleMap; a exceção não autoriza adicionar provider.
entries.availabilityReason: Além de Scene_Map, aceita uma cena cujo constructor.name seja Scene_EventedTitleMap. Criar essa cena exige um plugin externo.

entries.title: Dialogs e encerramento desktop após erro de idiomas
entries.context:
Requires Coreto_0_CoreEngine followed by Coreto_1_MessageCore. Use the MZ event editor for event commands and text; configure plugin defaults through the Coreto parameter authoring interface. Illustrative variable/event/asset IDs must exist in the project. Set /Localization/Enable=true, Languages=["English"], LangFiletype="csv", CsvFilename="Languages.csv", DefaultLocale="English". Put UTF-8 Languages.csv at the game root with exactly two lines: Key;English then Greeting;Hello. Each row must match the header width; the minimal valid table does not require the template full language set. Column names/keys cannot be empty or duplicate after trim/lowercase normalization. CSV delimiter is semicolon; TSV delimiter is tab. Quoted cells may contain the delimiter, and doubled quotes represent a quote; quotes must enclose the whole cell. Physical newlines inside cells are rejected: use
. LF/CRLF accepted, bare CR rejected, initial BOM removed. Current textLocale selects a case-sensitive language header; keys normalize to lowercase/trim. Missing key produces undefined, missing/empty selected cell UNDEFINED!, with no translation fallback. Serve the game through its normal HTTP/NW.js runtime. Enabled localization with a nonempty Languages list loads the configured root basename. HTTP success accepts status 200..399, parses before marking ready, and boot waits for ready. Network, timeout (30000ms), bad HTTP status or malformed table enter an error state; isDatabaseLoaded exposes LoadError with filename/reason and a retry callback. Correct the file/configuration/server first, then use the error-screen retry; a replacement request aborts the prior pending request and stale completions are ignored. Runtime never creates, converts or overwrites language files. CLI validation is available via message api describe MSG-BEH-language-write-boundary --json.
entries.expected: Fluxo original confirm/alert/SceneManager.exit não governa recuperação no browser. Erro claro impede boot e permite nova tentativa após correção, sem fechar o browser.
entries.availabilityReason: Adaptação/exclusão de desktop expressamente decidida pelo usuário; geração/conversão preservadas na CLI.

examples.input: If configured Languages.csv is missing, restore the minimal Key;English / Greeting;Hello table at the game root, validate it with message language validate --format csv --name Languages.csv --json, then retry the game load.
examples.expected: Boot proceeds only after the corrected table loads and parses successfully; a repeated failure remains an explicit load error.

entries.title: Criar, converter e validar tabelas de idioma
entries.context:
Execute a CLI com --project apontando para o jogo MZ. Nomes devem ser basenames com extensão .csv ou .tsv, sem subpastas; o destino de create/convert não pode existir. CSV usa ponto e vírgula, TSV usa tabulação, ambos em UTF-8. A primeira coluna deve ser Key e as seguintes nomes de idiomas, sem nomes ou chaves vazias/duplicadas; todas as linhas devem ter a mesma quantidade de células. Use
em vez de quebras físicas dentro de células. --format e --name explícitos evitam depender dos nomes configurados em Localization. Depois de criar ou converter, configure Localization.Enable, LangFiletype e CsvFilename/TsvFilename para carregar a tabela no jogo; a CLI não ativa essa configuração automaticamente.

entries.availabilityReason: Criação, conversão e validação de arquivos estão disponíveis pela CLI offline.

entries.title: Integração própria Coreto e Message
entries.context: Keep Coreto_0_CoreEngine before Coreto_1_MessageCore, RPG Maker MZ 1.10.0, the delivered filenames and refreshed plugin description/version markers. message install configures the already delivered Message bundle; it does not patch an arbitrary third-party runtime. The runtime checks engine version, duplicate Message provider, Core order, Message description/basename and declared consumer versions/order. Diagnostics identify failures with MESSAGE_ENGINE_VERSION, MESSAGE_DUPLICATE_PROVIDER, MESSAGE_CORE_REQUIRED, MESSAGE_DESCRIPTION, MESSAGE_FILENAME or MESSAGE_DEPENDENCY_VERSION/CONSUMER_ORDER. The bridge retains text conversion/drawing hooks, authored-code receivers, movement easing, formatted text measurement, serialized plugin-command dispatch aliases and picture-text sprite ownership/disposal for its compatible consumers. Use the corresponding public command/tag contracts rather than calling private bootstrap functions. Exactly one provider implements Message; compatibility flags are not additional implementations.

entries.availabilityReason: Ative o plugin indicado e suas dependências no jogo. Disponibilidade descreve a capacidade, não verifica a configuração do projeto.
